messages:
anya: Heads-up — after switching the RAG eval harness to the new quant4-fast kernel, we're seeing a spike in hallucination where retrieved docs are ignored and the model invents facts. Not classic hallucination — it's truncation + incorrect citation. sample: 'According to the doc, X => Y' but doc doesn't contain Y.
sam: ugh. is this only on long-context prompts or across board? any perf numbers?
anya: Mostly >6k token prompts (long code+docs). latency improved ~20% but F1 on citation detection drops from 0.92 -> 0.73 on our QA eval.
lina: do we have diffs vs fp16 baseline on the same eval set? could be tokenizer alignment or kv-cache bug after quantization.
anya: I ran a small A/B: same prompts, same chunking. fp16 keeps citations correct. quant4-fast fails more on passages with lots of punctuation/newlines.
devin: can you paste the serving config? I'm wondering if the chunking/stride changed with new kernel heuristics.
anya: config snippet:
```yaml
model: q4_fast_v2
chunk_size: 2048
stride: 512
kv_cache: enabled
compile_args:
  optimize_attention: true
```
sam: that chunk_size/stride seems fine. two possibilities: (1) quant kernel miscomputes attention for tokens around newline boundaries, (2) subtle tokenizer mismatch when we rebuild tokenizer with fast-bpe. lina any ideas from labeler side?
lina: If model emits different whitespace tokens, our citation matcher (regex + token offsets) can mis-align, causing us to mark it as hallucination. But you said it invents facts — that's different. We should capture raw tokens for a few failing cases.
anya: good call — attached outputs show token stream; I'll drop raw tokens into the repro gist.
devin: I'll add an end-to-end trace with KV cache dumps for a couple failing examples. ops-bot can you run a small canary against prod-like infra? 50 long prompts, compare q4_fast_v2 vs fp16.
ops-bot: scheduled canary: run_id=canary-1860000001-01, started, nodes=3, ETA ~8m. Results will post here.
sam: parallel ask: can we get labeler team to relabel ~200 RAG-specific failures into a small 'rag-edge' set so we can track regression metrics separately? need guidance on labels: false_citation, lost_context, truncation_halluc.
lina: we can spin up a relabel job. prefer to keep batches small (20 each) and include raw tokens + retrieved doc snippets. I'll own the schema and recruitment.
anya: thanks. also, let's add adversarial synthetic cases: nested code blocks + inline citations — those trigger the kernel most.
devin: timeline? if canary nails it as regression, we need to rollback quant kernel or patch compile args. ops-bot will post results soon.
ops-bot: canary complete. summary: q4_fast_v2 vs fp16 on 50 long prompts: citation_accuracy 0.68 vs 0.91; avg_latency 120ms vs 150ms.
anya: that's pretty conclusive. sam/lina — please kick off the relabel as priority. devin — can you repro locally with full KV dump and file a bug to runtime?
sam: starting relabel job: job_id=rl-1860000001, batch_count=10, items_per_batch=20, expected completion ~36h.
lina: added labeling instructions in the job: steps + examples + 'why it fails' section.
devin: filed runtime ticket RT-18602 with attached KV dumps and sample transcripts.
anya: action items recap:
- sam/lina: relabel job rl-1860000001 (rag-edge) — deliver annotated set + basic metrics
- devin: reproduce + runtime issue (RT-18602)
- ops-bot: keep canary scheduled against other variants (q4_safe, q8)
- anya: prepare eval PR to add rag-edge to CI and gates on citation_accuracy
I'll follow up in ~24h, thanks all :thumbsup:
